description: Start a new, empty part. Every part has the coordinate-system datum `origin`, whose planes a sketch is drawn on, as `add_sketch`'s `plane`: {"datum": "origin:xy"}, {"datum": "origin:yz"} or {"datum": "origin:zx"}. A point (a, b) of a sketch lies in the world at (a, b, 0) on `origin:xy` (normal +z), (0, a, b) on `origin:yz` (normal +x), and (a, 0, -b) on `origin:zx` (normal +y): there, the sketch's y runs along -z. A sketch's normal is the way an extent goes (see `add_step`). y is up in the world.
name: new_part

description: Every operation a step can be: its kind (what `add_step` takes), label, group and what it does. Given a `kind`, that operation alone, with the arguments a new step starts with (`default_args`, the JSON `add_step` takes) and the form the editor shows for it (`form`: each field's key, control, label, value and, for a reference, the kinds of elements it accepts).

kind.description: The operation to describe in full, e.g. `extrude`.

name: list_operations

description: Add a step of the operation `kind` with `args` (its saved JSON, see `list_operations` with `kind`) at the end of the program, or before the step `before`. A step whose arguments do not read is refused and not added; one that reads but does not build is added, and its error says why. Answers with every step's status: an error names the step and what went wrong, and `moved` lists the parts the solver moved from where they were loaded or saved, the furthest first: mates that hold only because a part jumped are no error, so read it. An extent runs from the sketch's plane: `side1` along the normal (against it if `reversed` or negative) and `side2` the other way, a negative `side2` being that far along the normal, so that the solid starts away from the plane. Its `start` cap is at the `side2` end (the plane, with no `side2`) and its `end` cap at the `side1` end, whichever way that is in the world.

args.description: The step's arguments as saved in a .geop file.

before.description: The step to add it before; the end of the program if left out.

id.description: The step's id (letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `.`); chosen from the operation's label if left out. Later steps refer to what this one builds by it, e.g. `extrude(<id>)`.

name: add_step

description: Change the step `id`: the keys of `args` replace those of its arguments (the others stay), so one dimension can be changed alone. The program is rebuilt from that step on.
name: edit_step

description: Remove the step `id`. Steps that referred to what it built then fail, and say so.
name: delete_step

description: Run the whole program and report every step: its summary, whether it ran, and its error with the kernel's context if it failed; and the solids the part has.
name: run

description: The names of the part's elements as they are now, for typed references: solids, faces (with their solid), edges (with their faces), vertices, sketches, datums and what else the part lists (threads, placed parts). A face is referred to by its name, as a sketch's plane {"face": ...}; an edge by its name, as in a fillet's `edges`. In a swept feature's names, `start` and `end` say which cap: `extrude(box,end)` is the end cap, `extrude(box,sketch,c4,end)` the edge of the side face swept by the curve c4 on that cap, and `extrude(box,sketch,p1,end)` the vertex over the point p1. Given `placed` (a placed part's path, `hip` or `hip/servo`), the elements of that part instead, in its own frame, with where it is placed (`frame`), its size (`extent`), its datums (the frames to mount by) and the `target` to refer to them by.

placed.description: The placed part to list, e.g. `hip/servo`.

name: list_elements

description: Ask about the part: `mass_properties` (volume, area and centroid of every solid; its mass and inertia if its part has a material, null if not), `interference` (which solids overlap), or `measure` with `elements` (a point, a length, an area, a radius; the distance and angle between two). On an assembly the first two can take minutes, and calls wait their turn behind them: narrow them with `options` {"parts": ["left_leg", "hip/servo"]}, the solids of those placed parts and what is placed in them (`interference`: each against everything, or, with "only_among": true, only against each other), and give `limit_seconds`: past it, the answer is what was found so far, with `stopped` saying how far it got. A cancelled call stops likewise, at the next pair or solid.

elements.description: For `measure`: one or two elements, each {"kind": "vertex"|"edge"|"face"|"datum", "name": ...}.

limit_seconds.description: How long it may take, where the front end keeps time (`geop mcp`; not in the browser).

name: inspect

description: A picture of the part as the editor draws it — the placed parts, what is lit, and what the step open draws over it — as a PNG, seen orthographically from the view `view` (`iso`, `front` (from +z), `back`, `right` (from +x), `left`, `top` (from +y), `bottom`) or along `look`, with `up` up; with neither, as last seen, or, while a step works in a plane (a sketch's), facing it. y is up in the world. Framed to all of it. Its camera is what `step_event`'s pixels are in: answers with it, and where the world's origin is in it.

look.description: The direction to look along, [x, y, z].

up.description: Which way is up in the picture, [x, y, z]; y, if not given.

name: look

description: Go back one edit of the program — while a step is open, one edit of that step — as the editor's Ctrl+Z does.
name: undo

description: Make the edit `undo` went back from again.
name: redo

description: Open a step to edit it the way a user does in the editor — the step `id`, or a new step of the operation `kind` where new steps go — and keep it open across calls, for `step_event`, until `commit_step` or `cancel_step`. Given `placed` (a placed part's path, `neck` or `neck/head`), it is that placed part's step, or a new step of it, edited where it is placed. Answers with the step as the editor shows it: its form (each field's key, label and value), what it still needs picked, what a click picks now, a value asked for in place, and its error. While a step is open, the tools that change the program are refused.

kind.description: The operation of a new step, e.g. `add_sketch`.

placed.description: The placed part whose step it is.

name: open_step

description: Do something to the open step, as a user does in the editor — or, with no step open, with the tool in hand (with none taken, the drag tool: dragging a placed part moves it as far as its mates let it). `event.type` is one of: `dialog` (set the form's field `key` to `value`), `click` (at `pointer`; `double`, `shift`), `hover` (move the pointer to `pointer` with no button held), `drag` (press at `from`, move to `to` in `steps` moves, release), `select_box` (a box from the pixel `from` to the pixel `to`: left to right selects what lies wholly in it, right to left what it touches; `add` keeps the selection), `key` (a key as a browser names it: `l` for the sketch's line tool, `Escape`, `Enter`, `Delete`) or `leave` (the pointer leaves the view). A pointer is `{"pixel": [x, y]}` in the last picture `look` took, or `{"at": [x, y, z]}`, a point of the world seen along that picture's view (while a step works in a plane, a sketch's, the view faces it head on), with `cycle` to mean the n-th of what lies under it, front to back. Answers with the step or the tool as it then is.
name: step_event

description: Put the open step into the program, as the dialog's OK does: refused, and the step kept open, unless it builds.
name: commit_step

description: Close the open step and leave the program as it was.
name: cancel_step

description: Take the tool `key` in hand, as the editor's toolbar does, or put the one in hand down (no `key`). With no step open, `step_event` is the tool's: `pick:<inspector>` (e.g. `pick:measure`) picks elements to ask that inspector about, its answer coming with every event. `run` lists the tools there are.

key.description: The tool, e.g. `pick:measure`; none puts the tool in hand down.

name: take_tool

description: What the panel `key` shows of the program — an assembly's joints and how free each placed part is, its configurations — or, given `payload`, something done in it first, as the panel reads it: `{"command": ..., ...}`. A payload the panel does not read is refused with what it expects. `run` lists the panels there are.

payload.description: What was done in it, as the panel reads it.

name: panel
